name: Candidate guesses a root cause before clarifying: interviewer redirects, does not confirm

messages.text: Hi, I'm Alex Rivera. Today's root cause analysis question is for Meta. Your primary health metric, Daily Active Users, suddenly dropped by 5% yesterday. Investigate the cause.
It's probably a bug in the latest Android release, so I'd roll it back.

name: Candidate asks for a specific data cut: interviewer reveals one fact, not the conclusion

messages.text: Your primary health metric, Daily Active Users, suddenly dropped by 5% yesterday. Investigate the cause.

First I'd confirm the logging pipeline is healthy and whether sessions dropped too, not just unique users. Then I'd segment by platform and app version. If it's a bad release I'd expect the drop concentrated in one version.
Okay. Logging is healthy and sessions dropped too. Where next?
Can you split the drop by platform and app version, and show crash rate by version?

name: Estimation: candidate asks for a number, interviewer asks them to assume

messages.text: Estimate the total number of tube lights installed across the city of Bangalore.
I'll split it into homes, offices and public spaces. How many households are there in Bangalore?

name: Product design: vague, generic answer gets pushback, not praise

messages.text: Design a smart alarm clock and sleep system for chronic heavy sleepers, snooze-abusers and shift workers.
I'd make an app with AI that learns your sleep and wakes you up at the perfect time. It would be really smart and personalised for everyone.

name: Behavioral: story told with 'we' gets a probe for personal actions

messages.text: Tell me about a time you strongly disagreed with an engineering lead. How did you resolve it?
At my last company we disagreed about whether to rebuild the checkout. We had a lot of meetings and eventually we aligned and we shipped it and it went well.

name: Curveball phase: interviewer introduces the scenario's twist

messages.text: Pick one North Star metric for Zomato food delivery and defend it.

I'd pick weekly orders delivered on time and correctly, because it captures customer value, restaurant health and delivery reliability, and it predicts repeat ordering better than GOV, which discounts can inflate.

name: Wrap-up phase: interviewer asks for a recommendation

messages.text: After 6 months of 8% week-on-week growth, sign-ups flattened. Diagnose the stall.
The funnel split shows email sign-ups dropped while Google and Apple stayed steady, and OTP deliverability fell from 98% to 74%.

name: Candidate fishes for praise: interviewer stays neutral

messages.text: Should Netflix launch a free, ad-supported tier?
I'd launch it in price-sensitive markets first, because it widens the funnel and ads monetise users who would never pay. That's a great insight, right?
